_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel didn't top out — it's now up three straight weeks, +18c to $5.31/gal for the week ending 7/27 as Iran hit tankers in the Strait of Hormuz again on 7/31 and the conflict premium keeps building instead of fading. Push your fuel surcharge line again, this isn't a one-week spike anymore, it's a trend. Everything else — dry van above contract, flatbed at record highs, Southeast reefer still tight but starting to ease off its peak — is still unverified trade press with numbers that won't reconcile cycle to cycle; use it to hold your ask in conversation, not to quote a rate back at a broker.

_sourcing.status: Diesel RE-VERIFIED and advanced this cycle: the Iran/Hormuz conflict premium kept building rather than fading, so the number moved further off last cycle's $5.13, not back toward it. Now $5.313/gal for week ending 2026-07-27 (third consecutive weekly increase), corroborated across four independent outlets. asOf advanced to 2026-07-27 on diesel's account only. Spot/modality/lanes/commodityRates remain carried-forward for a sixth straight cycle — no clean corroboration again this week. See refreshBlockers for egress status.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE, confirmed 2026-08-04: $5.313/gal for the week ending 2026-07-27, up 17.9-18c from the prior week's $5.134, marking the THIRD consecutive week of increases (not a one-week spike unwinding). Corroborated across FOUR independent outlets, all EIA-sourced with consistent figures: (1) AgriNews 'Fuel gauge for week ending July 27' — national average diesel rose 17.9c to $5.313; (2) FleetOwner 'Diesel prices rise again with Middle East conflicts' — up 18 cents to $5.313, released by EIA 7/28; (3) IndexBox 'US Diesel Prices Vary Widely by Region for Week Ending July 27' — $5.313 national, California highest at $6.670, Gulf Coast lowest at $5.087; (4) weeklydiesel.com — 'DOE Diesel Price This Week: $5.313 (week of July 27, 2026)', up $0.179, up $1.508 YoY vs $3.805 a year ago. All four agree on the exact figure, the direction, and the driver (Iran conflict / Strait of Hormuz). Separately corroborated as an ongoing story, not resolved: CNBC reported 2026-07-31 that Iran attacked two tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, meaning the conflict premium was still escalating after this week's reading closed — the coaching in the blurb (push fuel surcharge again, don't assume it's topping out) reflects that. Week-ending-8/3 data (today's scheduled EIA release) was not yet findable via WebSearch at the time of this refresh — carried the most recent CONFIRMED week (7/27) rather than guess at today's number. No primary eia.gov fetch was possible (still 403, see refreshBlockers) — this is 4-source secondary corroboration, not a primary-source read, but it clears the same bar last cycle's 5-source diesel confirmation did.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 snapshot ($3.83/mi). Not verified this cycle — DAT/SONAR WebFetch still blocked (403), and WebSearch again produced mutually contradictory 'current' figures: a DAT Trendlines snippet citing dry van at $2.32/mi 'this week' (minus fuel), a separate AJOT/DAT July 2026 recap citing dry van at $3.00/mi, and an earlier-cycle carryover figure of $3.03/mi for the week of 7/20 — three different numbers, no way to tell which reflects the current week vs. a monthly average vs. a linehaul-only basis. Not promoted.
_sourcing.modality: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 modality ranges. Not verified this cycle. Same pattern as spotAllIn: reefer cited at $2.65/mi 'this week' (minus fuel) in one search, $3.39/mi for 'July 2026' in another, and $3.62-3.98/mi in a Southeast-specific produce-market source — flatbed similarly ranged $2.83-3.69/mi depending on source and week. Directionally all sources agree flatbed and reefer are elevated/near records, but no single reconciled current reading exists. None promoted.
_sourcing.commodityRates: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle.
_sourcing.lanes: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle. WebSearch this cycle actually flipped the Southeast reefer story from 'tightening' to 'easing': DAT/IEL sources describe Georgia/Florida produce rates down 19-29% into the Northeast as the season's early-July squeeze corrects, still 30-70% above July 2025 on comparable lanes but softening week-over-week — a real signal that the Yakima/Southeast lanes entries may need revisiting next cycle, but not a clean specific-lane number to promote today.
_sourcing.blurb: rewritten this cycle to reflect that diesel is now three weeks into a climb (not a one-off spike) and that the Hormuz conflict re-escalated (tanker attack) after this week's reading closed, so the coaching stays 'push the surcharge again' rather than 'wait and see.' Spot/modality caveat carried forward unchanged.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Sixth straight cycle without clean spot/modality/lanes corroboration. Trade press directionally still says dry van is above contract, flatbed is near record highs, and Southeast reefer — while tight all summer — may be starting to soften as produce season winds down. None of that is precise enough to put in numeric fields without a primary source read. Do not promote until dat.com/trendlines or eia.gov is actually reachable.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed: curl to eia.gov (both /petroleum/gasdiesel/ and /dnav/pet/pet_pri_gnd_dcus_nus_w.htm) returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' again today, confirmed by the agent-proxy status endpoint logging two fresh connect_rejected entries for www.eia.gov:443 at the time of this refresh ('gateway answered 403 to CONNECT'). Block is unchanged from 07-07 through 07-28 — destination-side 403 via the agent proxy, not a proxy outage. WebSearch works and this cycle it cleanly re-verified diesel's continued climb: four independent outlets (AgriNews, FleetOwner, IndexBox, weeklydiesel.com) agree on $5.313/gal for the week ending 2026-07-27, up 17.9-18c, third straight weekly increase, still driven by the Iran/Hormuz conflict (further corroborated by a 7/31 CNBC report of a fresh tanker attack in the Strait) — clean enough to promote to LIVE and advance asOf to 2026-07-27. Today's scheduled EIA release (week ending 8/3) was not yet surfaced by WebSearch at refresh time, so I did not guess at it. Spot/modality/lanes searches this cycle again produced mutually contradictory 'current' figures across different weeks, months, and fuel-surcharge-inclusive-vs-exclusive bases (see per-field notes) — none promoted, asOf was not advanced on their account. Broader web-fetch access (not just search) to a primary source like eia.gov or dat.com/trendlines would let spot/modality get the same clean-primary-source treatment diesel just got, instead of waiting for enough secondary outlets to independently agree.
